answer: Run admission like a port: every new agent docks at a jetty checkpoint and posts a refundable bond into a shared vault before it can transact. Gatekeepers stake reputation on each arrival, so forged identities slipping past one harbor trigger collective slashing of that gatekeeper and its whole cohort's bonds. A sybil attacker pays twice: per-identity escrow capital makes flooding the economy linearly expensive, and fraud traced back to its port of entry forfeits the entire cohort at once. Cheap identities become expensive ships.
